opposingBeliefs: Raising minimum wage helps all low-income workers
Minimum wage increases have no downsides
Companies can easily afford higher wages
mainClaim: Raising minimum wage accelerates automation adoption and reduces entry-level employment opportunities for low-skilled workers
evidence: Jardim and coauthors (American Economic Journal: Economic Policy, 2022) studied Seattle's minimum wage increases to as much as $11 in 2015 and $13 in 2016, using Washington State administrative data. Relative to outlying regions of the state, aggregate hours worked at wages under twice the original minimum declined, though part of that reflects jobs moving above the wage threshold. Tracking individual workers, they found no change in the probability of continued employment but significant reductions in hours, particularly for less experienced workers. They estimate aggregate employment elasticities in the range of -0.2 to -2.0.
supportingPoints: One-time automation cost ($35k kiosk) becomes cheaper than ongoing higher wages over 2-3 years
Small businesses with thin margins (3-5%) struggle more than large corporations
Entry-level positions provide skills/experience ladder; fewer positions = fewer opportunities
Automation displaces workers who then compete for even fewer remaining jobs
Benefits concentrate among workers who keep jobs; laid-off workers worse off
limitations: The cited paper studies employment and hours in Seattle. It does not study automation or kiosk adoption, so the link from minimum wage to automation is not established by this source. Studies show mixed results across different cities and timeframes. Some research finds minimal employment effects. Doesn't account for benefits to workers who keep jobs and earn more. Correlation vs causation issues - automation trends exist independently. Small sample sizes in some studies. Short-term vs long-term effects differ.
counterCounterArguments: Gradual phase-ins can minimize shock and allow businesses to adjust
Increased consumer spending from higher wages can offset costs
Some automation would occur regardless of wage levels due to technology advancement

sourceMetadata.title: Minimum-Wage Increases and Low-Wage Employment: Evidence from Seattle
sourceMetadata.methodology: Synthetic control on aggregate hours plus matched longitudinal analysis of individual workers
